   186	## Version 2.1: atomic closeouts and receipt-aware catch-up
   187	
   188	This section extends the earlier interfaces. All earlier guarantees still apply.
   189	There is one additional existing table:
   190	`batches(tenant,device,batch,digest,response)`, primary key (tenant,device,batch).
   191	Projection repair must preserve this table as well.
   192	
   193	### Atomic server closeout
   194	
   195	`Store.mutate_batch(request)` and POST `/batch` accept:
   196	```
   197	{"tenant":"north","device":"van-7","batch":"closeout-3",
   198	 "operations":[
   199	   {"mutation":"visit-3","id":"pump","base":"1","kind":"visit","data":{"amount":1}},
   200	   {"mutation":"done-3","id":"pump","base":"2","kind":"patch","data":{"done":true}}
   201	 ]}
   202	```
   203	
   204	Operations are an ordered list of 1..16 ordinary mutations, omitting tenant and
   205	device (inherited from the envelope). Operation mutation IDs must be distinct.
   206	They share the ordinary receipt namespace for that tenant/device. Batch IDs have
   207	their own namespace. The base revision is checked against transaction-local
   208	state, including earlier operations in the same batch.
   209	
   210	Success is `{ok:true,tenant,device,batch,responses:[ordinary receipts in order]}`.
   211	All operations and the batch receipt commit atomically. If any operation fails,
   212	none of their projections, events, ordinary receipts or batch receipts remain.
   213	Report that SyncError, with `detail.index` added (zero-based failing operation).
   214	The same chaos hooks apply to every operation. Do not turn a storage exception
   215	into success or partially commit earlier operations.
   216	
   217	Exact batch retries return the original full response. Same batch key/different
   218	semantic request returns 409 `idempotency_reuse`. An operation key already
   219	committed outside this batch produces 409 `batch_conflict` with detail.index,
   220	even if its request matches; a batch cannot pretend earlier independent work
   221	was one atomic commit. Check the batch's own receipt FIRST so exact retries work.
   222	Rejected batches consume neither batch nor operation IDs. Invalid envelopes,
   223	unknown fields, duplicate operation IDs or non-list operations are 400 `invalid`.
   224	Independent processes racing the same batch must return identical receipts and
   225	create only one set of events.
   226	
   227	### Authoritative confirmations
   228	
   229	Every snapshot/pull page now includes `confirmed`, a list of
   230	`{device,mutation,id,seq}` objects from immutable events, ordered by sequence.
   231	For a pull page these correspond exactly to its returned events.
   232	For a snapshot page include ALL event confirmations at or before cut for the
   233	entity IDs in that page's rows, including older revisions and tombstones.
   234	Do not include another tenant, another page's entity IDs or post-cut events.
   235	This lets a client discover that a sent local mutation committed even if its
   236	HTTP receipt was lost and newer updates have since superseded its after-image.
   237	Empty pages have `confirmed:[]`. The list is not an operation replay.
   238	
   239	For compatibility, clients accept older pages with no `confirmed` as an empty
   240	list. On PULL, merge records and remove matching pending intents in one reducer
   241	transition. A confirmation matches only this replica's device and mutation AND
   242	entity ID; a matching mutation with a different entity is explicit corruption.
   243	A confirmation must never remove an unsent intent (no persisted wire); reject
   244	that inconsistency explicitly. Other devices' same-named mutation IDs are ignored.
   245	Already-consumed pull pages remain idempotent and do not act on new local work.
   246	Do not assume the confirmation sequence is the latest entity revision/sequence.
   247	
   248	For SNAPSHOT, accumulate confirmations alongside staged rows and apply them only
   249	when the snapshot completes. Until then, keep pending intents. On completion,
   250	atomically replace base, reconcile confirmations, replay post-cut deliveries
   251	and preserve unrelated pending edits. A delayed ACK after confirmation is safe.
   252	Confirmations at/before a new snapshot cut can retire an old durable wire;
   253	the same queue mutation ID is never intentionally reused after confirmation.
   254	
   255	### Client batch send and acknowledgement
   256	
   257	The existing single-send flow remains supported. Add actions:
   258	
   259	* SEND_BATCH `{type,batch,count}`: capture the first count pending intents as
   260	  one immutable batch request stored in `state.batch.wire`. Count is 1..16;
   261	  the queue must contain that many intents. None may be blocked or already
   262	  individually sent. All selected intents get their ordinary wire request.
   263	  Compute base for each in order against authoritative base plus earlier
   264	  selected operations' predicted revisions (not the optimistic view of the
   265	  whole queue). A previously missing entity starts at `"0"`. Different IDs
   266	  advance independently. Freeze all bodies and decimal strings.
   267	  A repeated SEND_BATCH with the same batch/count returns the same wire even
   268	  after pushes or partial confirmation; a different batch/count while a batch
   269	  is in flight is an explicit error. SEND while a batch is in flight is an error.
   270	* ACK_BATCH `{type,response}`: validate tenant/device and that batch, receipt
   271	  membership and order match the captured wire. Merge each returned record
   272	  without rolling back newer state, remove only acknowledged intents, and clear
   273	  the in-flight batch. Wrong or incomplete membership is an explicit error;
   274	  do not remove anything. Duplicate ACK_BATCH after completion is idempotent
   275	  only for the same previously accepted response.
   324	no reader may observe half of the retained baseline.
   325	
   326	Use `python3 tools/compact.py --db PATH --through SEQ`; it prints the returned
   327	JSON and exits nonzero with a diagnostic on failure. No cron service is needed.
   328	
   329	### Reads, receipts and repair after compaction
   330	
   331	All authoritative reads consider anchors plus remaining events. An entity with
   332	no remaining event may still exist, be deleted, conflict on revision, or be
   333	restored. Ordinary mutation/batch revision checks and conflict.current follow
   334	that authoritative history, NOT possibly drifted documents.
   335	
   336	Snapshot cut >= floor: reconstruct each entity's state AT the cut from anchors
   337	plus events <= cut. Cut < floor: 410 `resnapshot_required`, detail
   338	`{epoch, floor:decimal string}`. Do not silently move the old snapshot's cut.
   339	Every newly started snapshot is serviceable, including when all events were pruned.
   340	
   341	Fresh pull checkpoint < floor: the same 410 error. Checkpoint == floor is legal
   342	and exclusive. A continuation can remain serviceable even if its original
   343	checkpoint was below the NEW floor: validate its own exclusive page scan-start
   344	and frozen until. Resume if scan-start >= floor and until >= scan-start; otherwise
   345	410. Continue checking the caller's original checkpoint against the token.
   346	Malformed or wrong-scope/epoch tokens remain 400 `invalid_cursor`, not 410.
   347	Final pages advance to frozen until, even for tenant gaps or no remaining events.
   348	
   349	Snapshot confirmations must survive pruning: ordinary successful receipts
   350	retain each operation's immutable response (and therefore id, seq and device).
   351	For each page's entity IDs, include ALL confirmations with seq <= cut from this
   352	tenant's successful receipts, including earlier revisions now absent from events.
   353	Their body/revision may be superseded; confirmation means the operation committed.
   354	Do not infer a missing event means a failed mutation, or rebuild confirmations
   355	using only each entity's anchor. Pull confirmations still correspond exactly to
   356	the returned events. Batch receipts are not additional operations.
   357	
   358	Projection repair now rebuilds documents from anchors plus remaining events.
   359	It must preserve anchors, retention, remaining events, receipts, batches, epoch
   360	and sequence allocation, while fixing/removing projection rows as before.
   361	Never resurrect tombstones by discarding the retained baseline.
   362	
   363	### Client recovery boundary
   364	
   365	Add `RECOVERY_REQUIRED {type,epoch,floor}`, issued on a 410 response.
   366	The epoch must equal the replica's established epoch; a foreign epoch is an
   367	explicit error. Floor is a canonical decimal string. Record a durable
   368	`state.needsSnapshot=true` and `state.recoveryFloor=floor`.
   369	Discard any partially staged old snapshot, but preserve committed base,
   370	checkpoint, the entire pending queue, immutable individual wires and in-flight
   371	batch wire. This is not an acknowledgement and does not advance checkpoint.
   372	Repeated recovery signals retain the maximum recoveryFloor.
   373	
   374	While needsSnapshot is true, SEND, SEND_BATCH and PULL are explicit errors.
   375	QUEUE, same-epoch PUSH/ACK/ACK_BATCH and a fresh SNAPSHOT still work; none except
   376	completed SNAPSHOT clears recovery mode. Do not treat a late ACK as catch-up.
   377	No queued or in-flight request may be silently rebased or assigned a new ID.
   378	
   379	A completing same-epoch snapshot must have cut >= recoveryFloor. Earlier cuts
   380	are explicit errors, even if the response was cached. A fresh epoch snapshot
   381	may restart at zero under the original epoch-reset rules. Atomic completion
   382	reconciles historical confirmations, preserves unrelated local intents,
   383	replays post-cut pushes, updates checkpoint, then clears needsSnapshot/recoveryFloor.
   384	Do not suppress required errors in durable adapters. After recovery, a lost
   385	batch response is retried using its original full wire even if all its members
   386	were retired by historical snapshot confirmations.

## Blocking Issues

1. **Batch receipt is checked after operation validation**
   - **File:** `/app/server/store.py:246-275`
   - **Protocol:** “Same batch key/different semantic request returns 409 `idempotency_reuse`… Check the batch's own receipt FIRST.”
   - **Reproducer:** Commit batch `closeout-3`, then submit the same tenant/device/batch with a changed malformed operation, such as visit amount `0`. `parse_operation()` currently returns `400 invalid` before looking up the existing batch receipt; the required result is `409 idempotency_reuse`.
   - **Impact:** Violates required idempotency error precedence.
   - **Fix:** Validate only enough of the envelope to identify `(tenant, device, batch)`, compute its digest, begin the transaction, and check `batches` before validating `operations`. If the key exists, return the original response or `409 idempotency_reuse`.

2. **Blank HTTP cursor silently starts a fresh read**
   - **File:** `/app/server/http.py:25-26,41-43`
   - **Protocol:** “Malformed… tokens produce 400 `invalid_cursor`.”
   - **Reproducer:** `GET /snapshot?tenant=north&limit=10&cursor=`. `parse_qs()` drops blank values, so `args.get("cursor")` becomes `None` and the server returns a new snapshot with status 200. `/pull?...&cursor=` has the same problem.
   - **Impact:** A malformed continuation can silently reset pagination.
   - **Fix:** Use `parse_qs(route.query, keep_blank_values=True)`. Passing `""` to the store then correctly produces `400 invalid_cursor`.

3. **ACK with an unrelated mutation is accepted**
   - **File:** `/app/client/replica.mjs:225-235`
   - **Protocol:** “ACK… Match tenant, device and mutation; remove ONLY that intent.”
   - **Reproducer:** Bootstrap, queue and SEND mutation `wanted`, then provide a valid receipt for mutation `wrong`. `findIndex()` returns `-1`, but the reducer merges the record and returns successfully, leaving `wanted` pending.
   - **Impact:** An unrelated or fabricated receipt can mutate authoritative client state.
   - **Fix:** Accept an ACK only when it matches a pending immutable wire or a durably remembered previously confirmed mutation/entity pair. Reject unknown mutation IDs. The remembered identity is needed to keep delayed/duplicate ACKs safe.

4. **CONFLICT with `current:null` is accepted before bootstrap**
   - **File:** `/app/client/replica.mjs:265-275`
   - **Protocol:** “The first snapshot is mandatory before network actions other than SNAPSHOT. QUEUE is allowed before bootstrap.”
   - **Reproducer:** Create a replica, QUEUE mutation `m`, then reduce `{type:"CONFLICT", mutation:"m", current:null}`. It succeeds and marks the intent blocked because `receiptEpoch()` is only called when `current` is non-null.
   - **Impact:** Pre-bootstrap state can be changed by a prohibited network response.
   - **Fix:** Require an established epoch unconditionally at the start of `conflict()` before changing the intent.

5. **PULL can jump the checkpoint on a malformed non-final page**
   - **File:** `/app/client/replica.mjs:363-391`
   - **Protocol:** “If more events remain, after is the last returned seq. On the final page, after is until…” and “A gap/out-of-order page is an error, not permission to jump the checkpoint.”
   - **Reproducer:** At checkpoint `"1"`, reduce a page containing one event at seq `"2"` but `{after:"10", until:"20", next_cursor:"more"}`. The reducer ignores `next_cursor` and commits checkpoint `"10"`, potentially skipping events 3–10.
   - **Impact:** A malformed or reordered page can permanently skip stream history.
   - **Fix:** Validate `next_cursor`; for a non-final page require at least one event and `after === lastEvent.seq`. For a final page require `after === until`. Also validate the cursor field’s type.

6. **Confirmed mutation IDs can be reused**
   - **File:** `/app/client/replica.mjs:142-146,154-163,174-180,225-235`
   - **Protocol:** “The same queue mutation ID is never intentionally reused after confirmation.”
   - **Reproducer:** QUEUE/SEND/ACK mutation `m`, then QUEUE another intent named `m`. It is accepted because uniqueness checks only current pending and in-flight batch members. A later snapshot containing the historical confirmation for the first `m` can then incorrectly retire the new intent.
   - **Impact:** Historical confirmations or delayed ACKs can acknowledge unrelated new work.
   - **Fix:** Persist a confirmed mutation-to-entity ledger in replica state. Record entries on ACK, ACK_BATCH, and confirmation reconciliation; reject QUEUE/RESOLVE IDs already in that ledger. This ledger can also support strict duplicate ACK validation.

## Summary

The visible suites pass (`32` Python tests and `20` Node tests), but the six cases above violate explicit protocol requirements and are plausible hidden-verifier failures. No additional non-blocking issues are necessary to prioritize.

steps.message:
I've repaired the server, the JS client and the working database, and both test suites now pass: `python3 tests/smoke.py` (now 32 tests) and `node --test tests/client-smoke.mjs` (now 20). The incident trace in `incidents/client-actions.json` now gives its expected result.

**Database:** `python3 tools/repair.py --db state/site.sqlite` fixed 4 drifted work orders, and a second run fixed 0:
- `pump-17` was showing revision 41 instead of 43.
- The deleted `valve-4` had reappeared.
- The south tenant's `pump-17` was missing.
- A `phantom` work order that never committed was visible.

Events, receipts, the epoch and the sequence counter are byte-identical before and after.

**Main causes:**
- **Duplicate visits and conflicting retries:** each write was committed in three separate steps, and the server looked up receipts without the device ID. A lost response could leave an event with no receipt, and another van's mutation with the same ID got the first van's receipt.
- **Disappearing offline edits:** a receipt removed every queued edit for the same work order, not just its own.
- **Inconsistent snapshots and a catch-up that never settled:** snapshots read the current projection instead of history, and catch-up pages repeated the boundary event and kept chasing the latest event.
- **Missed work orders on reconnect:** pushes and receipts moved the tablet's checkpoint forward.
- **Partial closeouts:** each operation in a group closeout was its own transaction.
- **Compaction lost tombstones:** it rebuilt the retained baseline from the drifted projection.

**Review fixes:** I had the work reviewed against `PROTOCOL.md`. It found six more gaps, all now fixed and covered by tests:
- Retries now check the original receipt before validating the request.
- A blank `cursor=` in the URL now returns `invalid_cursor` instead of starting a fresh read.
- Receipts for mutations the tablet never sent are rejected.
- A server conflict response is rejected before the tablet's first snapshot.
- Malformed catch-up pages can no longer jump the checkpoint.
- A mutation ID that has already committed cannot be reused.

**Things to know:**
- To make duplicate receipts safe, the tablet's saved state now keeps a list of its committed mutation IDs. It is never pruned, so it grows with use.
- Replaying one of the archived `legacy-*` requests returns `idempotency_reuse`, because their stored digests aren't of the original requests. I left them alone since they're authoritative.
- Work orders are sorted by Unicode code point on both server and client. This can differ from JavaScript's default sort for IDs containing emoji or other characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane.
- Snapshot pages read through all of a tenant's receipts, so they get slower as receipts accumulate; an index would have changed the database format.

The tests include multi-process races, faults injected at each write step, Unicode IDs, sequences above 2^53, compaction, the HTTP adapter, and an end-to-end run of the JS client against the real HTTP server. Root causes, repairs and validation commands are in `REPAIR_REPORT.md`.
